note: Session 17: Four system prompt fixes + SQL bug fix in get_route_day_summary. Targets: wrong stop attribution on route_overview results, cross-route 'latest bus' hallucinations, disambiguation context loss, and false no-service for routes with non-standard stop_sequence.

vision.statement: An AI-powered transit assistant for Gainesville RTS riders that understands plain-language questions and guides the customer to the right answer — whether that's a real-time ETA or a scheduled departure time.
vision.cx_journey: Customer arrives at the assistant and types a question in plain language (e.g. 'When does the next 75 leave Butler Plaza?'). The assistant leads the interaction — asking clarifying questions when needed — until it can deliver the specific ETA or schedule information the rider needs.
vision.wizard_strategy: The Trip Wizard is the conversation flow prototype. It makes the decision tree explicit (intent → route → stop → direction → result) in a structured UI so the paths can be validated. Once proven, the same guided logic is translated into the chat assistant's prompting — the AI replicates the wizard's flow in natural language instead of button clicks.
vision.end_state: A single assistant interface where any RTS rider can ask a transit question in plain English (or Spanish) and get a reliable, accurate answer without needing to know stop IDs, route numbers, or schedules.

summary.goal: Deliver a stable Gainesville RTS backend with realtime bus info, schedule support, and a user-facing web assistant/dashboard.

tasks.title: P1-A: Label real-time vs static schedule in every response
tasks.details: Research finding: users trained by Google Maps expect all answers to be real-time. When we return a GTFS schedule time they treat it as an ETA — trust collapses when bus doesn't match. tasks.title: P1-B: Add human escalation after 2-3 consecutive failures

Options: (A) Expand stop_areas.json with known Gainesville landmarks mapped to specific stop IDs — low cost, limited coverage. (B) Add Google Places / OSM geocoding call to find nearest GTFS stop to a described location — broader coverage, adds external API dependency. tasks.title: Tool-Use Refactor: Design tool schema (inputs, outputs, status codes)
tasks.details: Define the 5 tools the LLM will call instead of the current rule-code pipeline. Each tool must return an explicit status field — never empty arrays. Tools: (1) search_stops(name_or_landmark) → [{stop_id, stop_name, match_type}] or {status: 'no_match'}. (2) get_realtime_predictions(stop_id) → [{route, minutes, headsign}] or {status: 'no_service' | 'api_unavailable'}. (3) query_schedule(route_id, stop_id_or_name, time?, date?) → [{departure, headsign}] or {status: 'no_trips' | 'stop_not_found' | 'route_not_found'}. (4) get_routes_at_stop(stop_id) → [{route_id, headsign}]. (5) get_route_overview(route_id, date?) → {first, last, frequency_min, directions[]} or {status: 'no_service'}. Document inputs/outputs/status codes before writing any code.

tasks.title: Tool-Use Refactor: Implement tool wrapper functions
tasks.details: Create routes/agent_tools.py. Wrap existing services as clean tool-callable functions matching the schema from tooluse-1. Each wrapper: (1) calls the existing service (schedule_service, rts_api, stop_resolver) — no new business logic. (2) Always returns an explicit status so the LLM never sees ambiguous empty results. (3) Handles exceptions internally and returns {status: 'error', message: ...} rather than raising. Keep all existing service code untouched — this is just a translation layer. Depends on: tooluse-1.

tasks.title: Tool-Use Refactor: Write the system prompt with grounding rules
tasks.details: Write the system prompt that defines what the LLM is, what it can do, and what it must never do. Must include: (1) Persona: RTS Gainesville transit assistant. (2) Hard grounding rule: ONLY state departure times and stop names that appear in a tool result from this conversation. Never use training knowledge about bus schedules. (3) No-hallucination rule: if a tool returns no results or an error, say exactly that — do not guess or interpolate. (4) Tool-call-first rule: always call a tool before answering any factual transit question. (5) Language rule: respond in the language the user wrote in (EN/ES). (6) Brevity rule: 3 sentences max, preserve times/routes/stop IDs exactly. Can be written in parallel with tooluse-2.

tasks.title: Tool-Use Refactor: Build the tool-use agent orchestration loop
tasks.details: Create routes/agent_v2.py with a single handle_message(msg, history, session_ctx) function. Pattern: (1) Build messages array from history. (2) Call LLM with tools defined. (3) If response has tool_calls: execute each tool, append results to messages, call LLM again. (4) Repeat until no tool_calls (max 5 iterations to prevent loops). (5) Return final text answer + any button suggestions the LLM emits. LLM choice: gpt-4o-mini (already integrated, existing _openai_client() helper reused). Temperature = 0 for all tool-synthesis responses. Depends on: tooluse-2 and tooluse-3.

tasks.title: Add find_route_coincidences tool to v2 agent
tasks.details: Add a 6th tool: find_route_coincidences(route_ids: list, date?, tolerance_minutes?=5). GTFS JOIN query: stop_times for route A × stop_times for route B at same stop_id, filtered by ABS(departure_time_A - departure_time_B) <= tolerance. Returns list of {stop_name, stop_id, route_A_time, route_B_time, diff_minutes}. Answers 'when are routes 1 and 20 at the same stop?' Currently the agent hallucinates an answer by pattern-matching first/last times from get_route_overview — verified in testing.

tasks.title: GPT-driven scenario testing infrastructure for v2 agent

(4) gpt_user_simulator_prompt.md — paste-into-ChatGPT prompt that makes GPT generate 30+ new realistic rider queries + 5 multi-turn chains, formatted to match scenarios_v2.json schema for direct appending. Workflow: run script → paste results into GPT (judge) → paste task suggestions back to Claude (fix) → repeat.

tasks.title: Fix: get_route_day_summary returned false no-service for some routes
tasks.details: Session 17: SQL query in get_route_day_summary used `stop_sequence = 1` (hardcoded) to find each trip's first stop. GTFS routes whose trips don't start at sequence 1 returned zero rows and were reported as runs_today=False. Fixed by adding trip_first_seq CTE using MIN(stop_sequence) per trip — now works for any starting sequence value. Likely caused 'no trips for Route 75 today' when Route 75 was verifiably running.

tasks.title: Fix: Agent incorrectly attributed route_overview times to named stops
tasks.details: Session 17: get_route_overview returns first/last departure from each trip's origin stop (stop_sequence=1), not from named terminal stops like Rosa Parks. LLM was saying 'departs from Rosa Parks at 11:13 PM' for a Route 1 trip whose headsign was 'To Rosa Parks' (meaning Rosa Parks is the destination). Added ## INTERPRETING get_route_overview RESULTS section to SYSTEM_PROMPT in agent_v2.py.

tasks.title: Fix: 'Latest bus running today' cross-route comparison now correctly out-of-scope
tasks.details: Session 17: 'What is the latest/last bus running today?' requires comparing all routes simultaneously — the per-route tools cannot answer it. Added this as an explicit example in ## WHEN THE QUESTION IS BEYOND YOUR TOOLS. Agent now honestly says it can't answer instead of hallucinating per-route results and inventing 'no trips' for routes it didn't verify.

tasks.title: Fix: Agent forgot time/date params after disambiguation exchange
tasks.details: Session 17: When user said 'it doesn't matter' after being shown multiple stop options, LLM forgot time specified in original query (e.g. 'noon') and called get_schedule with current time. Also: when user corrected the wrong time ('I said noon, not 8pm'), agent called search_routes instead of retrying get_schedule. Added ## HANDLING DISAMBIGUATION RESPONSES section: pick first candidate, preserve all original params (time/date/route/kind), do NOT call wrong tools on corrections.

tasks.title: Re-run full scenario test suite after session-17 fixes
tasks.details: Run `python tests/run_v2_scenarios.py --env local` to validate session 17 fixes. Target 28+/30 pass. S12/S13 may now pass (BEYOND YOUR TOOLS updated). M01/M02/M04/GPT13/GPT15 multi-turn empty responses still need investigation.

tasks.title: Fix 6 system prompt gaps found via tool schema audit
tasks.details: Session 18 (commit 4fce616): (1) kind=first/last is day-level — 'first bus after 4pm' must use kind=next+time, not kind=first; (2) get_realtime_predictions returns ALL routes — added rule to filter displayed results to user's specified route; (3) skip search_stops when user gives a numeric stop ID; reuse resolved stop_ids within conversation; (4) date format must be single-word day name or ISO — never 'next Monday'; (5) no_trips auto-calls get_route_overview to show when route does run instead of dead-ending to customer service; (6) direction filter improved: two-step headsign exclusion (stop name + downtown hub equivalence: Rosa Parks = Downtown Station = RTS Transfer Center); ask user if ambiguous.

tasks.title: Fix: direction filtering for 'out of [stop]' queries — needs new approach
tasks.details: Problem: 'first bus 1 out of Rosa Parks after 4pm' returns BOTH headsigns — 'To Downtown Station' (4:01 PM) AND 'To Butler Plaza' (4:06 PM). User expects only 'To Butler Plaza' since Rosa Parks IS the downtown hub. What was tried and failed: (A) System prompt rules (Step 1: exclude headsigns containing stop name, Step 2: downtown hub equivalence Rosa Parks=Downtown Station=RTS Transfer Center) — LLM ignores it reliably. (B) filter_inbound boolean parameter on get_schedule schema — LLM still decides, same reliability problem. Current state: automatic Python-level _filter_inbound_departures() added to agent_tools.py (commit 426e68b) — applies on all hub stops without LLM involvement, but NOT yet validated. Approach to investigate: (1) Verify if automatic hub filter actually works on prod — run test query. (2) If not, look at GTFS direction_id field per trip — Route 1 at Rosa Parks direction_id=0 vs direction_id=1 may deterministically identify outbound vs inbound without string matching. (3) Consider adding direction as a separate field in the tool result so the LLM can reason about it more reliably. (4) Consider always returning the stop's full name in results so headsign comparison is exact.

tasks.title: Fix: LLM omitted `time` param on get_schedule causing 'no departures' false negatives
tasks.details: Session 18: Root cause of 'route 1 after 4pm from rosa parks' returning no departures. Tool description said 'Omit to use current time' — LLM skipped the time param, tool returned current-clock departures (e.g. 10:42 AM), LLM compared those to user's '4pm' window and concluded no trips. Proved by exact match of 'hallucinated' times to dispatch_tool output with no time arg. Fix: (1) agent_tools.py time param description now says 'ALWAYS pass this when user mentioned a specific time'; (2) agent_v2.py SYSTEM_PROMPT CRITICAL rule added explaining that omitting time defaults to current clock and will produce wrong results. Commit a3dbd33.
